newsitem.title: INDIA: BSE chief to meet India finance minister next week.
newsitem.headline: BSE chief to meet India finance minister next week.

text.p: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Tuesday it will make a presentation to India's finance minister next week about the depressed state of the country's stock exchanges.
"The time for action has come and the measures to boost the markets must come as a comprehensive package," BSE President M.G. Damani told a news conference.
The net decline in the BSE's market capitalisation from the time of India's annual budget announcement on July 22 to October 4 was around 1,440 billion rupees ($40.4 billion), Damani said.
He said nearly 50 percent of the 6,690 scrips listed on the Bombay bourse were trading below par.

The benchmark Bombay stocks index has fallen some 18 percent since July 22 and brokers say several measures introduced in Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's budget, including the imposition of a 12.9 percent minimum tax on previously untaxed company profits, have hit the markets.
Weak market conditions have forced most companies to raise money through debt issues.

"State Bank of India is bringing down its prime rate but at the same time corporates are raising interest rates (on their fixed deposits) to attract sufficient money for their schemes. It clearly reflects the corporate fear that if they don't raise money now they will be unable to in the coming months," Damani said.
India's largest commercial bank cut its prime lending rate to 15.5 percent from 16.0 percent per annum in September.
